title: api: improve rate-limit semantics, idempotency handling, and retry-after for streaming & OpenAI compat
author: Aisha Khan
description: Motivation: Requests hitting rate limits or transient capacity issues have historically produced inconsistent responses across the OpenAI-compat layer and native Redwood endpoints. Streaming endpoints in particular could terminate mid-stream without a deterministic error envelope or Retry-After guidance, causing client SDKs to retry incorrectly and creating duplicate resource side-effects for non-idempotent operations. This change standardizes rate-limit semantics and idempotency handling across the API surface, aligns behavior with OpenAI compatibility expectations, and adds guardrails for streaming and function/tool calling flows. What this PR does (single continuous description): - Add and standardize Retry-After behavior for 429 responses across REST and streaming endpoints. When we return 429 we now always include a Retry-After header (seconds) and a JSON error body with a consistent error structure. Streaming 429s will emit a terminal SSE/event with the error envelope before closing the stream. - Introduce idempotency-key support for non-idempotent create endpoints (chat/completions/create, embeddings bulk create, tool-invoke endpoints). The server will accept Idempotency-Key headers and deduplicate requests server-side for up to 24h. We document the semantics (at-most-once for successful commits, at-least-once best-effort for in-flight cancels). - Normalize error payloads to the schema {"type":"rate_limit|server_error|invalid_request", "code":"string", "message":"string", "param":"string|null"}. This is applied to both REST and streaming terminal events to make SDK parsing deterministic. - OpenAI compatibility layer changes: map Redwood internal rate limit buckets to OpenAI-like error codes and ensure the 429 -> Retry-After translation follows a consistent seconds-based semantics (instead of ms). Add compatibility flag that ensures responses include fields expected by popular SDKs (error.type -> error.name mapping preserved). - Streaming stability: ensure chunk bookkeeping on the server when a client-sent idempotency-key is present. If a stream is interrupted due to rate limit or server OOM, the final event includes the standardized error envelope and the same idempotency key is associated with the terminal state so retrying clients can rehydrate or deduplicate properly. - Tool/function-calling: when a tool invocation fails due to transient infra (429/503), we return a structured error and include a recommended retry strategy in the error.meta.retries field (string values: "none", "immediate", "exponential_backoff"). Tool timeouts are surfaced via error.code = "tool_timeout" and include a human-friendly message. - Observability: add metrics for idempotency hits/misses, retry-after observed, streaming-termination-reasons, and compatibility-mapped-429s. - Docs & SDK: update OpenAI-compat docs and examples for idempotency header usage, and add tests in the SDK integration matrix to validate Retry-After parsing and streaming terminal envelopes. Implementation highlights: - Runtime: added a new rate_limit middleware that computes Retry-After seconds and injects it into responses. Streaming pipeline now supports terminal envelope emission before socket close. - Idempotency store: lightweight dedupe table in Redis with TTL 24h and a small in-process write-ahead cache for low-latency lookups. - Error normalization: central error serializer that maps internal errors to the public schema. Backwards-compatibility code in openai_compat module maps legacy "name" fields. - Tests: end-to-end tests added for: 1) streaming 429 produces terminal JSON event with Retry-After header; 2) duplicate create with same Idempotency-Key returns stored response and does not double-side-effect; 3) mapping of internal rate buckets to OpenAI compatibility codes. Rollout plan and migration notes: - Feature flag gated behind "api.rate_limits.strict_retry_after" for 2 weeks. Gradual rollout to production with monitoring dashboards for unexpected client errors. - SDK releases (python/typescript/go) pinned to the compatibility mode by default and include idempotency header helpers. - No immediate breaking changes expected; error payload shape is an additive normalization. Existing clients that introspect raw error fields should switch to the documented schema. Backcompat & edge cases: - If an Idempotency-Key is missing, behavior remains the same (best-effort at-most-once for completed operations where possible). - For streaming clients that do not expect a terminal JSON event, we added telemetry and a short deprecation notice in docs; the server will still close the socket after emitting the terminal envelope so clients that ignore it will simply see a close. References: linear ENG-1284, ENG-1350; internal incident SUP-4421 (streaming termination during burst).

review_comments: Ravi: Can we guarantee Retry-After will always be seconds and never fractional? Response: yes, we round up to nearest second and document this. Added helper to ceil the computed value.

Leah: Is the 24h TTL for idempotency okay for large payloads? Response: we kept a small footprint (hash -> response metadata) and will revisit if customers request longer windows. TODO: add admin TTL override.
Tomás: Suggest exposing idempotency metrics in console with per-customer breakdown. Response: added idempotency_hits_total and idempotency_misses_total counters with tenant labels.
Emi: Confirmed OpenAI compat mapping preserves legacy error.name for older SDKs. Response: added compatibility flag and migration docs.
Leah: CI flaky test in e2e suite. Response: reran pipeline and adjusted test timing to avoid intermittent network races.
Ravi: Approve after address minor nits in log messages.
release_notes: Standardize 429 Retry-After semantics (seconds) for REST and streaming endpoints.
Add Idempotency-Key support for non-idempotent create endpoints with 24h dedupe window.
Normalize public error payloads to a structured schema for easier SDK parsing.
Improved streaming stability: terminal error envelope emitted before stream close.
